contract: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are compositions {'formula': str, 'composition': {element: amount}}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and RDKit are importable (pandas and torch only where the environment provides them; they are not requirements of the task); wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric
notes: Official Matbench v0.1 data (SHA-256 equal to matminer's recorded hashes) and folds. Reference check: the stored per-fold predictions of the published AMMExpress v2020 and RF-SCM/Magpie submissions rescored with this evaluator's folds and metric reproduce their leaderboard MAEs exactly (validation/chemistry-checks.json).
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Matbench: experimental band gap from composition
description: Predict the experimentally measured band gap (eV) of 4604 inorganic compounds from their composition alone. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.
benchmark: Matbench: experimental band gap from composition
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Zhuo, Mansouri Tehrani and Brgoch (2018): predicting band gaps of inorganic solids by machine learning from composition; source of the measurements.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Polymorphs with the same composition share one value (deduplicated by composition), and 53% of the entries are metals with zero gap; the source states no licence.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.
